why: MegaMan's CurAction while he uses a chip is the chip's family in both games: BN4's a state of his (BN4_PLAYER_STATES 0x080EAEFC by the record's +0xB, run with his object in r5; the state makes r7 the attack's variables itself, his AI data's +0x70: the spread family's 0x080EC762-0x080EC764), BN6's an attack family (BN6_ATTACK_FAMILIES 0x080EBFA0 by the number less 0x10, run by RunAIAttack with r7 the variables, his AI data's +0xA0: BN6's twin family 0x25 reads them at 0x080EDEF4 with no load of its own). A unit of BN4's chips' code of the kind 'attack' is one of BN4's states moved whole into BN6's grown attack families at a number of BN4's chips' own (src/emu/xattack_grow.h XATTACK_BN4, 0xD0 on; tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py ATTACK_NUMBERS), which its chips' records take as their family with BN4's own subfamily (src/core/xchips_record.c xrec_from_bn4). So BN4's family in his CurAction and in the action his saved state keeps is read as that number, by the units' rows (XCHIP_ATTACK, BN4's family, the number); his attack's subfamily is BN4's own in both and is left as it is (a registry row whose `sub` is 0xD0 or over names the family, not a support routine).
